text:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT ALERT: Cluster eu-ny-onprem-3 - sustained inference queue growth. alert: queue_length > 500 for 18m, pending_pods=42, scheduling_failures due to Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu. Pager routed to @oncall-eng.
Mia L: I'm taking initial triage. acknowledging pager, will gather impact and start mitigation.
Sam R: Thx. quick ask — which customers on this cluster? severity estimate?
Raj P: Affected: AcmeHealth (private-dedicated), BetaAI (VPC-peered), internal e2e smoke tests. Error rates start spiking ~15:12 UTC. Rolling 5m error increase ~22% for BetaAI.
Mia L: Symptoms: autoscaler logs show repeated node provision attempts that time out. pending pods stuck in Pending for >10m with "0/4 nodes available: 4 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu".
Mia L: Pushing a short snippet of kubectl describe for a pending pod:
```
Name: inference-worker-7f9c8
Namespace: redwood-prod
Status: Pending
Message: 0/4 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----    ------            ----  ----               -------
  Normal  PodScheduled      12m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ... to eu-ny-nodepool
  Normal  Pulling           11m   kubelet            Pulling image "..."
  Warning FailedScheduling  10m   default-scheduler  0/4 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```
Raj P: Also posting scaledown/scaleup autoscaler log tail:
```
[autoscaler] 15:08 attempt_scale_up target=10 current=4
[autoscaler] 15:09 provision_request sent: 6 nodes
[provisioner] 15:12 ProvisionTimeoutError: node bootstrap timeout after 900s
[autoscaler] 15:12 mark_provision_failed reason=NodeProvisionTimeout
[autoscaler] 15:12 no further attempts: capacity_provider=onprem-baremetal max_nodes_reached=false
[autoscaler] 15:13 queue_length=512
```
Kevin H: Looks like provisioner hits BMC/IPMI timeouts. we've seen the 'bootstrap timeouts' on this rack after hardware firmware updates. Might need manual intervention with the on-site provisioning orchestrator.
Sam R: Customer impact: BetaAI reports ~20% request failures and long tail latencies up to 6s. AcmeHealth has degraded throughput but no data loss; queued requests piling.
Mia L: Short-term mitigation options:
• Route non-sensitive traffic to hosted fallback (requires opt-in/consent for private customers) via smart-routing policy.
• Bump up autoscaler parallel_provision_limit and retry_backoff to attempt more simultaneous node boots (risky if underlying failure persists).
• Manual cold-start of spare nodes via on-site provisioning (coordinate with infra ops).
Tanya S: I'll draft a customer-safe fallback note. For AcmeHealth we need legal/ops signoff before routing outside VPC. BetaAI is ok with cross-region failover per their SLA; we can flip a subset of classes.
Mia L: I'm going to try incremental measures: 1) raise parallel_provision_limit from 2->6 (temporary), 2) enable fallback routing for BetaAI only, 3) open infra escalations channel. Doing that now.
ops-bot: change_request: autoscaler.parallel_provision_limit updated from 2 to 6 by Mia L at 15:22 UTC. change_id=CR-8341
Mia L: Executed step 1. autoscaler accepted new config. Monitoring provisioning logs.
Raj P: Seeing new provision attempts. logs show a few successes then again ProvisionTimeout on node3.
Raj P: Log snippet:
```
[provisioner] 15:25 request node-7 booting
[provisioner] 15:28 node-7 healthy
[provisioner] 15:31 request node-8 booting
[provisioner] 15:36 ProvisionTimeoutError: node-8 no response from BMC
```
Kevin H: Node hardware / BMC flakiness confirmed. Ops on-call paged to attend rack 3. ETA 28m for on-site tech. Recommend we limit new allocations to rack 1/2 which have healthy BMCs.
Sam R: Any chance of temporarily increasing existing nodes' GPU share? (container-level QoS tweaks?)
Mia L: Not safely for dedicated workloads — would risk noisy neighbors and violate isolation. We can however shift lower-prio jobs to hosted endpoints and free up GPU capacity for priority customers.
Tanya S: I've enabled fallback routing for BetaAI to hosted-dedicated-1 for 30% of traffic. BetaAI notified via support channel.
Mia L: After bumping parallel limit we recovered ~120 of the queued requests by routing and successful node boots. Queue now at 382 and dropping slowly.
Raj P: New metric: pending_pods down from 42 -> 26 in 10m. Error rate for BetaAI back to 6% (was 22%).
Mia L: On-call handoff to infra: Kevin H is taking over incident operations for hardware/provisioning. I'll stay until we confirm on-site fix. @Kevin H please ack and confirm next steps.
Kevin H: Ack. I'll coordinate with rack tech, disable faulty BMCs from rotation, and bring up spare nodes in healthy racks. Also opening ticket with vendor for firmware rollback if needed.
Mia L: Ops escalation: ESCL-527 opened and linked to this thread. Action items:
- Kevin: on-site BMC check + bring spares (ETA 28m)
- Mia: maintain routing to hosted for BetaAI, track customer impact
- Tanya: customer comms for AcmeHealth and BetaAI, note potential cross-VPC failover options
- Raj: keep monitoring autoscaler/provisioner logs + perf dashboards
Sam R: Good. Postmortem owners? Recommend infra lead + runtime SRE to co-own.
Mia L: Assigning postmortem to Kevin H + Raj P. Due EOD tomorrow.
ops-bot: incident_update: status=mitigated provisional_recovery=true queued_requests=312 participants=[Mia L, Kevin H, Raj P, Tanya S]
Mia L: Tagging handoff: I'm marking this as "operational handoff" at 15:38 UTC. Kevin, taking the incident primary.
Kevin H: Took primary at 15:38 UTC. Continuing to coordinate hardware. Will post final update when nodes stable or on-site confirms firmware action.
Tanya S: I'll update customers with current mitigation and next steps. Draft to BetaAI and AcmeHealth in support threads now.
Mia L: Thanks team. Follow-ups: verify autoscaler backoff settings, add an automated monitor to flag BMC flakiness across racks, and add a runbook step to restrict provisioning to healthy racks when BMC errors exceed threshold.
Sam R: Thx. Leaving notes for postmortem: root cause likely on-site BMC/firmware causing node bootstrap failures -> autoscaler backoff + parallel limit interactions -> queue surge. Recommend tiered fallback policies and pre-warmed spares.
Kevin H: Update 15:53 UTC: on-site confirmed BMC NIC firmware mismatch. Redeploying firmware to 4 nodes; expected 40m until stable. Spares started in rack2.
Mia L: Last status (15:59 UTC): queued_requests=128, pending_pods=9, BetaAI error rate ~1.8%. I'll close pager and move to follow-up channel. Thanks all.
ops-bot: incident_resolved: resolved_by=Mia L resolution_summary=Provision failures caused by BMC/firmware mismatch; temporary routing to hosted + manual spares reduced queue and customer impact. next_steps=postmortem + firmware patch rollout.
